justification.rationale: Every framework API used is the documented (and only) stable way to do the job, and TS 7 is a justified, low-risk dev-time win. The only unjustified item is the direct @lit-labs/ssr-client dependency, which serves no purpose in an app with no custom elements.

findings.issue: @lit-labs/ssr and @lit-labs/ssr-client are declared as direct dependencies but never imported by app code; @gracile/gracile@0.11.0 already provides @lit-labs/ssr transitively, and ssr-client is unused since the app has no custom elements to hydrate.
findings.suggestion: Drop both from dependencies and let Gracile supply the SSR engine transitively; if they must stay for peer-dep reasons, document why in a comment.

findings.issue: typescript ^7.0.2 uses the native Go rewrite that went stable only ~3.5 months ago (2026-07-08); a caret range will pull future 7.x behavior changes into a fresh major line.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable for a dev-only typecheck, but pin the minor (e.g. ~7.0.2) or note the choice, since TS 7 is a ground-up rewrite still early in its stable life.

findings.issue: Gracile is pre-1.0 (0.11.0), so the whole runtime stack inherits pre-stable semantics; any Gracile upgrade may break.
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact pin (already well done) and budget a pin-bump review on each 0.x release; the single-file adapter in server.js keeps the swap cheap.

summary: A deliberately conservative app: every API its own code touches is documented, stable-surface Gracile or long-stable web-platform code, with zero unstable/experimental flags. The only experimental dependency, Lit Labs SSR, is the mandated framework's own engine and is never imported by app source, though it's redundantly listed as a direct dep. Toolchain majors (Vite 8, TypeScript 7) are recently stable but not experimental, and the exact framework pin plus the one-file express adapter keep the pre-1.0 stack well contained.
